entities.name: Pepin the Short
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pepin the Short was the King of the Franks from 751 until his death in 768, marking the beginning of the Carolingian dynasty.

He played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval European political landscape, uniting various Frankish tribes and expanding his kingdom's borders through strategic alliances and military conquests.

Pepin's reign also saw the establishment of the Capetian dynasty, which would go on to produce notable French monarchs such as Hugh Capet and Louis VI.

Pepin's legacy extended beyond his own kingdom, influencing the development of the Holy Roman Empire and the Holy See, with his dynasty's members playing significant roles in the shaping of Western Christendom.

"For the love of God, I have fought for Christ, for the Church, and for the salvation of the people." - Pepin the Short, as quoted by the Frankish historian Einhard.
